buildMesh2D=buildMesh2D(mesh_type, x0, y0, lx, ly, nb_elem_x, nb_elem_y, vertices=None, number=None):

- mesh_type: type of mesh:

  - 'Q4': mesh with elements Q4
  - '2T3': mesh with elements T3, obtained by spitting one Q4 in two T3
  - '4T3': mesh with elements T3, obtained by spitting one Q4 in four T3 
  - 'Q8': mesh with elements Q8

- ly: dimension of the rectangle, following the axis Oy
- nb_elem_x: number of elements, following the axis Ox
- nb_elem_y: number of elements, following the axis Oy

- vertices=None: a given list of x,y-coordinates, following a suitable Q4-mesh node ordering
- number=None: index of the avatar (still present to ensure compatibility)

cubicLattice3D.doc:
coor=cubicLattice3D(nb_ele_x, nb_ele_y, nb_layer, l, x0=0., y0=0., z0=0.):

this function compute a list of positions on a cubic lattice

parameters:

- nb_ele_x: number of particles on the first layer, following axis (Ox) (the lowest)
- nb_ele_y: number of particles on the first layer, following axis (Oy) (the lowest)
- nb_layer: number of layers
- l: length of a lattice element, i.e. distance between two 
  consecutive positions on the same layer, or the same column

optional parameters:

- (x0, y0, z0): position of the lower left corner of the bounding box 
  of the lattice, i.e. the first position is (x0 + l/2, y0 + l/2, z0 + l/2)

return value:

- coordinates of the positions [nb_ele_x*nb_ele_y*nb_layer,3]

N.B.: the total number of positions is nb_ele_x*nb_ele_y*nb_layer

WARNING:

1. the maximal radius of the particles to be deposited max_radius must 
   verify: max_radius <= l/2
2. the dimensions of the bounding box of the lattice are :
   nb_ele_x*l x nb_ele_y x nb_layer*l

extrudeMesh.doc:
vol_mesh = extrudeMesh(m, lz, nb_lz=1):

This function returns the extrusion of an input linear mesh along z-axis.

parameters:  

- m: a 2D mesh
- lz: height of the extruded mesh
- nb_lz: number of layers to extrude

All elements are extruded:
  Point->S2
  S2->Q4
  T3->PR6
  Q4->H8

All elements of the original surface are kept on the surface at bottom and top.
All physical entities name are modified a 'E' is appended if the element is the
result of the extrusion, a 'B' is appended if the element is the original bottom
element and a 'T' is appended if the element is the top element of the original
surface.

granuloDoubleRoughWall.name: granuloDoubleRoughWall
granuloDoubleRoughWall.signature: (center, l, rmin, rmax, model, material, theta=0.0, color='WALLx', nb_vertices=0, seed=None)
granuloDoubleRoughWall.doc:
body=granuloDoubleRoughWall(center, l, rmin, rmax, model, material, theta=0., color='WALLx', nb_verices=0, seed=None):

this function builds a 2D rough wall: it returns a body made of a cluster
of disks or polygons. The radii of the particles defining the cluster are randomly distrubuted in the
interval [rmin, rmax]

parameters:  

- center: mass center of the wall  in the global frame
- l: minimal length of the wall, i.e. since the wall is made of
  disk having a given radius, it could be bigger than expected
- rmin, rmax: bounds of the interval of radii defining the roughness of the wall
- model: rigid model for the particle
- material: the particle is made of this material

optional parameters:

- theta=0.: rotation angle in the inertial frame
- color='WALLx': color of a disk contactor
- nb_vertices=0: if nb_vertices is greater or equal to three, generated particles are
  regular polygons having nb_vertices vertices
- seed=None: seed to use to control the randomness

rigidPolyhedron.name: rigidPolyhedron
rigidPolyhedron.signature: (model, material, center=array([0., 0., 0.]), color='BLUEx', generation_type='regular', nb_vertices=0, vertices=None, faces=None, radius=1.0, tol=0.0, number=None, seed=None, xr=1.0, yr=1.0, zr=1.0)
rigidPolyhedron.doc:
usage: 

body = rigidPolyhedron(model, material, center=numpy.zeros(3,'d'), color='BLUEx', generation_type='regular', 
                       nb_vertices=0, vertices=None, faces=None, radius=1., tol=0., number=None, seed=None, 
                       xr=1., yr=1., zr=1.)

This function builds a rigid convex polyhedron using 4 methods (see below).

Some parameters are common to the methods and mandatory:

- model : rigid model for the particle
- material : the particle is made of this material


Some parameters are common but optional:

- center=numpy.zeros(3,'d') : position of the center of inertia the particle in the global frame
- color='BLUEx' : color of the sphere contactor.
- generation_type='regular' : the method used to generate the polyhedron contactor.
- number=None: index of the avatar (still present to ensure compatibility).

Generation methods:

- First method (generation_type ='regular') consists in generating vertices of the polyhedron
  regularly disposed on a sphere (of radius 'radius'). For Platon's polyhedra (number of
  vertices is 4, 6, 8, 12 or 20) the number of vertices used is exactly the one given in input,
  otherwise the number of vertices found by the generator may differ from the one in input
  (especially for low number of vertices).

  parameters :  

  - nb_vertices=0. : number of vertices of the contactor
  - radius=1. : radius of the encompassing sphere.
  - xr=1., yr=1., zr=1. : sphere to ellispoid mapping

- Second method (generation_type ='random') consists in generating vertices of the polyhedron
  randomly disposed on a sphere (of radius 'radius'). The number of vertices used is exactly
  the one given in input (contrary to the first method).

  - nb_vertices=0. : number of vertices of the contactor
  - radius=1. : radius of the encompassing sphere.
  - tol=0. : tolerance to use to remove a vertex if the one found is to close to others (if 0. no check)
  - seed=None : seed to use to control the randomness
  - xr=1., yr=1., zr=1. : sphere to ellispoid mapping

- Third method (generation_type ='vertices') generates the polyhedron defined by the convex hull
  of the vertices given in input. The 'vertices' array may be modified on output if the vertices
  set given was not convex.

  - vertices=None : array of coordinates (nb_vertices,3), if the vertices set is not convex
    on input, some points will be deleted on output.

- Fourth method (generation_type ='full'|'bevel') generates the polyhedron using the vertices and
  connectivity given in input. Using 'bevel' will cut corners.

  - vertices=None : array of coordinates (nb_vertices,3).
  - faces=None: faces as triangles connectivity of vertices (nb_faces,3). Numbering of vertices
    in 'faces' array is 1 to nb_vertices (and not 0 to nb_vertices-1 like in Python).

A first line gives the number of rigids and 
the following lines give the corresponding indices in the BODIES.DAT file.
parameters:
   - command: a postprocessing comand
   - avatar2body: a dictionnary mapping an index of an avatar to 
                  the corresponding index in the BODIES.DAT file.
   - path: path to the POSTPRO.DAT file

writeRigidSets.name: writeRigidSets
writeRigidSets.doc:
writeRigidSets(command, avatar2body,path=''):
this function writes rigid sets in the POSTPRO.DAT file.
A first line gives the number of rigid sets. 
For each rigid set, a first line give the number of rigids in the set, and 
the following lines give the corresponding indices in the BODIES.DAT file.
parameters:
   - command: a postprocessing comand
   - avatar2body: a dictionnary mapping an index of an avatar to 
                  the corresponding index in the BODIES.DAT file.
   - path: path to the POSTPRO.DAT file

writeTC.name: writeTC
writeTC.doc:
writeTC(command,avatar2body,path=''):

parameters:

   - avatar2body: a dictionnary mapping an index of an avatar to

   - path: path to the POSTPRO.DAT file

writeTactyInBodies_MAILx.doc:
Allow to write a contactor container of a MAILx avatar in a file object

:param ensCont: the contactor container to write
:param ensGroup: the group container used by ensCont
:param dimension: the space dimension of the avatar

writeVlocRlocIni.doc:

:param with_xl: (optional) if using XL format

AddDof2InBodies.name: AddDof2InBodies
AddDof2InBodies.doc:
Change reference coordinates to current coordinates.
Usefull to generate a BODIES.OUT corresponding to current state.

Not available for 3D rigids!

AssembleMechanicalLHS.name: AssembleMechanicalLHS
AssembleMechanicalLHS.doc: Assemble the elementary matrices of mechanical deformable bodies.

AssembleMechanicalRHS.name: AssembleMechanicalRHS
AssembleMechanicalRHS.doc: Assemble the elementary right hand sides of mechanical deformable bodies.

AssembleMultiLHS.name: AssembleMultiLHS
AssembleMultiLHS.doc: Assemble the elementary matrices of multi-phasic deformable bodies.

AssembleMultiRHS.doc: Assemble the elementary right hand sides of multi-phasic deformable bodies.

AssemblePoroLHS.doc: Assemble the elementary matrices of porous deformable bodies.

AssemblePoroRHS.doc: Assemble the elementary right hand sides of porous deformable bodies.

AssembleThermalLHS.name: AssembleThermalLHS
AssembleThermalLHS.doc: Assemble the elementary matrices of thermal deformable bodies.

AssembleThermalRHS.name: AssembleThermalRHS
AssembleThermalRHS.doc: Assemble the elementary right hand sides of thermal deformable bodies.

CircularSelection.name: CircularSelection
CircularSelection.doc:
Select a subpart of a 2D sample to apply it post processing commands.

The subpart of the sample consists of all particles in a disk around a point.

parameters:

- x: abscissa of the center of the disk
- y: ordinate of the center of the disk
- r: radius of the disk centered on (x;y).

CloseDisplayFiles.name: CloseDisplayFiles
CloseDisplayFiles.doc:
Used to close containers of visualization files (*.pvd).
But no need anymore

ComputeBulk.name: ComputeBulk
ComputeBulk.doc:
Compute rigidity/conductivity elementary matrices and internal forces
for all bodies in the simulation.

ComputeDof.name: ComputeDof
ComputeDof.doc:
Compute current values of displacement from the current velocities computed
for all bodies in the simulation.

ComputeFext.name: ComputeFext
ComputeFext.doc:
Evaluate the sum of the external forces during the current time step (due to gravity and boundary conditions)
for all bodies in the simulation.

ComputeFreeVelocity.name: ComputeFreeVelocity
ComputeFreeVelocity.doc:
Compute velocity free of interactions for all mechanical bodies in the simulation.

The contact detection configuration is also computed then, except if a
the command 'Integrator_SetContactDetectionConfiguration' is used.

ComputeMass.name: ComputeMass
ComputeMass.doc:
Compute mass/capacity elementary matrices
for all bodies in the simulation.

ComputeRnod.name: ComputeRnod
ComputeRnod.doc:
Recompute the 'reac' value of each bodies
from the contact network (this storage)

DisplayOutDof.name: DisplayOutDof
DisplayOutDof.doc: Display the current values of all degrees of freedom in the simulation.

DisplayOutRnod.name: DisplayOutRnod
DisplayOutRnod.doc: Display the current values of reactions on all bodies.

DisplayOutVlocRloc.name: DisplayOutVlocRloc
DisplayOutVlocRloc.doc: Display the current values of every contacts.

ExSolver.name: ExSolver
ExSolver.doc:
Run Non-linear Gauss Seidel contact solver.

parameters:

- stype: type of solver ('Exchange Local Global' or 'Stored_Delassus_Loops').
- norm: type of norm ('Quad', 'QM/16', 'Maxm').
- conv: convergence tolerance demanded.
- relax: relaxation parameter.
- gsit1: maximum number of convergence check before stopping.
- gsit2: number of iterations of nlgs before checking convergence.

FatalDamping.name: FatalDamping
FatalDamping.doc: Compute fatal damping for all bodies.

FdSelectProxTactors.name: FdSelectProxTactors
FdSelectProxTactors.doc: Special way of computing sphere/sphere contacts.

Finalize.name: Finalize
Finalize.doc:
Close LMGC90.

If  the --no-finalize option is passed to the python interpretor
this function is skipped.

This is useful when wanting to use the python interpretor in
interactive mode after a computation and check LMGC90 database content.

IncrementStep.name: IncrementStep
IncrementStep.doc: Prepare a new time step computation.

InitHDF5.name: InitHDF5
InitHDF5.doc:
Initialize HDF5 output file (and use h5repack just in case)

If no filename given or HDF5 has not been used during compilation
this function is ignored and next calls to 'WriteOut' function
will write ASCII files in OUTBOX directory

Initialize.name: Initialize
Initialize.doc:
Initialize LMGC90 (and timers).

timer_GetNewTimer(xxx) must be called after this function.

LoadBehaviours.name: LoadBehaviours
LoadBehaviours.doc:
Load behaviours read in BULK_BEHAV.DAT in 
bodies read from BODIES.DAT.

Must be called after: ReadBehaviours and ReadBodies.

LoadModels.name: LoadModels
LoadModels.doc:
Load models read in MODELS.DAT in 
bodies read from BODIES.DAT and initialize property sets.

Must be called after : ReadModels and ReadBodies.
Must be called before: LoadTactors

LoadTactors.name: LoadTactors
LoadTactors.doc:
Load contactor modules from bodies.

Must be called after: ReadBodies, ReadIniDof and LoadModels if any mesh.

OpenDisplayFiles.name: OpenDisplayFiles
OpenDisplayFiles.doc:
Initialize visualization file writing.

Parameters:  

- restart (int)   : first index of file to write
- mecagp_field (list of strings) : the list of meca GP field to display ('strain' and/or 'stress')
- thergp_field (list of strings) : the list of ther GP field to display ('gradT' and/or 'fluxT')
- write_f2f (integer) : 0 do not write, 1 write only f2f, 2 also write central kernel, 3 add stress
- write_parameters (boolean) : True (default) write integer to string parameters mapping in separate file
- time_fmt (string) : format of the 'timestep' field written in the lmgc90.pvd file
                      (something like ".3f" for example but empty by default)

Path.name: Path
Path.doc:
PurePath subclass that can make system calls.

Path represents a filesystem path but unlike PurePath, also offers
methods to do system calls on path objects. Depending on your system,
instantiating a Path will return either a PosixPath or a WindowsPath
object. You can also instantiate a PosixPath or WindowsPath directly,
but cannot instantiate a WindowsPath on a POSIX system or vice versa.

ReadBehaviours.name: ReadBehaviours
ReadBehaviours.doc: Read TACT_BEHAV.DAT and BULK_BEHAV.DAT files in DATBOX directory.

ReadBodies.name: ReadBodies
ReadBodies.doc: Read BODIES.DAT file in DATBOX directory.

ReadDatbox.name: ReadDatbox
ReadDatbox.doc:
Read all .DAT and .INI files from DATBOX directory
to initialize LMGC90 database.

ReadDrivenDof.name: ReadDrivenDof
ReadDrivenDof.doc:
Read DRV_DOF.DAT file in DATBOX directory.

Must be called after ReadIniDof.

ReadIni.name: ReadIni
ReadIni.doc:
Read initial state

If compiled with HDF5 library, it can read from
the 'h5_file' input parameters.

Otherwise the function will try to read from OUTBOX directory

With HDF5, if 'record' is < 1, then last record is read.
With OUTBOX, if 'record' is -1, then .LAST are read.

ReadIniGPV.name: ReadIniGPV

ReadIniMpValues.name: ReadIniMpValues

ReadIniVlocRloc.name: ReadIniVlocRloc

ReadModels.name: ReadModels
ReadModels.doc: Read MODELS.DAT file in DATBOX directory and initialize external models.

ReadMpBehaviours.name: ReadMpBehaviours
ReadMpBehaviours.doc:
Read and load multi-physics (for rigids) behaviours.

What is disper ?

RecupRloc.name: RecupRloc
RecupRloc.doc:
Try to get back state of interactions from last stocked interactions.

In each contact module: verlet -> this. Must be called before SelectProxTactors.

If tol is given in input, PLPLx_RecupRlocByPosition is used. To use the
same type of function for PRPRx contact, use PRPRx_SetTolRecupRloc.

SelectProxTactors.name: SelectProxTactors
SelectProxTactors.doc:
Run detections if current time step number is a multiple of freq_detec.

In case of PRPRx contact, one of next functions must be called:

- PRPRx_UseCpCundallDetection
- PRPRx_UseCpF2fExplicitDetection
- PRPRx_UseCpF2fDetection
- PRPRx_UseNcDetection
- PRPRx_UseNcF2fDetection
- PRPRx_UseNcF2fExplicitDetection


Parameters:

- freq_detec (default 1) : frequency of particules neighbourhood recomputation during detection
- useExt (default 0) : set to 1 to use external detections of CLALp interactions (coupling with Xper)
- reset (default 0) : set to 1 to reset the detection and redo box computation

SetContactRadius.name: SetContactRadius
SetContactRadius.doc: Set the contact radius for spher/spher or cylinder/cylinder contacts.

SetDimension.name: SetDimension
SetDimension.doc:
Set dimension of the simulation and
type of simulation.

possible values of mod:

- 1 for PSTRAIN
- 2 for PSTRESS
- 3 for AXI

SetDomainBoundary.name: SetDomainBoundary
SetDomainBoundary.doc:
Set active domain boundary for rigid bodies.

Only: 

- 2D: x | y boundary
- 3D: x | y | z boundary

SetNumberInteractionByContact.name: SetNumberInteractionByContact
SetNumberInteractionByContact.doc:
Experimental: set the number of interaction by contact.

Available only for sphere/sphere and cylinder/cylinder contacts.

SetPeriodicCondition.name: SetPeriodicCondition
SetPeriodicCondition.doc:
Set periodic conditions for rigid bodies.

Only: 

- 2D: x period for DKDKx, DKDKL and PLPLx.
- 3D: x and y period for CDCDx, SPSPx, PRPRx and PTPT3

SmoothForceComputation.name: SmoothForceComputation
SmoothForceComputation.doc:
Explicit computation of the contact forces.

Not available for every contact types.

StockRloc.name: StockRloc
StockRloc.doc:
Stock state of interactions.

In each contact module: this -> verlet. Must be called after SelectProxTactors.

UpdateStep.name: UpdateStep
UpdateStep.doc:
Update state.

Current time step values become begin time step values.

WriteBehaviours.name: WriteBehaviours
WriteBehaviours.doc: Write materials and contact laws in ascii files (OUTBOX/BULK_BEHAV.OUT and OUTBOX/TACT_BEHAV.OUT).

WriteDisplayFiles.name: WriteDisplayFiles
WriteDisplayFiles.doc:
Write visualization files if current time step number is a multiple of freq in DISPLAY directory.

Parameters:

- freq (int)       : manages the occurence of file creation

Optional arguments are a tuple to add external fields to visualize in case a VTK.

Deprecated: the arguments 'ref_radius', 'normal_orient' and 'write_gp' are now useless and will be removed in a future release

WriteDrivenDof.name: WriteDrivenDof
WriteDrivenDof.doc: Write driven degrees of freedom in ascii file (OUTBOX/DRV_DOF.OUT).

WriteHDF5.name: WriteHDF5
WriteHDF5.doc:
Write HDF5 output.
- DOF (degree of freedom) in 2D and 3D
- Vloc_Rloc in 2D and 3D
- GPV fields

WriteLast.name: WriteLast
WriteLast.doc:
Write Last files.
If InitHDF5 has been used with a valid filename
then it will write in the defined file.
Otherwise the ASCII files in OUTBOX directory will
be written

WriteLastDof.name: WriteLastDof
WriteLastDof.doc: Write last degreees of freedom values in ascii file (OUTBOX/DOF.LAST).

WriteLastGPV.name: WriteLastGPV
WriteLastGPV.doc: Write last Gauss points values in ascii file (OUTBOX/GPV.LAST).

WriteLastMpValues.name: WriteLastMpValues
WriteLastMpValues.doc: Write last mp values in ascii file (OUTBOX/MP_VALUES.LAST).

WriteLastRnod.name: WriteLastRnod
WriteLastRnod.doc: Write last nodal reaction in ascii file (OUTBOX/Rnod.LAST).

WriteLastVlocRloc.name: WriteLastVlocRloc
WriteLastVlocRloc.doc: Write last interactions values in ascii file (OUTBOX/VlocRloc.LAST).

WriteMpBehaviours.name: WriteMpBehaviours
WriteMpBehaviours.doc: Write Multi-physics ascii file in OUTBOX directory.

WriteOut.name: WriteOut
WriteOut.doc:
Write Out files.
If InitHDF5 has been used with a valid filename
then it will write in the defined file.
Otherwise the ASCII files in OUTBOX directory will
be written

WriteOutDof.name: WriteOutDof
WriteOutDof.doc:
Write degrees of freedom of current time step in ascii file (OUTBOX/DOF.x.OUT where 'x' is the rank of the file)
if current time step number is multiple of nsteps.

WriteOutGPV.name: WriteOutGPV
WriteOutGPV.doc:
Write current Gauss points values of all meshes (OUTBOX/GPV.x.OUT)
if current time step number is a multiple of nsteps.

WriteOutMpValues.name: WriteOutMpValues
WriteOutMpValues.doc: Write multi-physics data at current time step in ascii file(s).

WriteOutRnod.name: WriteOutRnod
WriteOutRnod.doc:
Write current values of reaction for each bodies if current time step number
is a multiple of nsteps.

WriteOutVlocRloc.name: WriteOutVlocRloc
WriteOutVlocRloc.doc: Write values of every interactions if current time step number is a multiple of nsteps.

addF2fToVtkBlocks.signature: (blocks, i_block, f2f_c, f2f_p, f2f_inters, inters, f2f_uf, cop_uf, cpc_uf)

addRegistersToDisplay.doc:
Decide to automatically add registered field to WriteDisplayFiles.

Parameters
----------
to_add : boolean
         To enable (default) or disable.

buildSegment.name: buildSegment
buildSegment.signature: (coorx, coory, coorz, nx, ny, nz, lr)

checkDirectories.name: checkDirectories
checkDirectories.doc:
Check if DATBOX directory exists (if not, it stops).
Create OUTBOX, POSTPRO and/or DISPLAY directory if one
does not exists.

checkInteractiveCommand.name: checkInteractiveCommand
checkInteractiveCommand.doc:
Check if some specific files exist and react depending on the result:

- file 'stop': write every possible .OUT files and exit.
- file 'save': write every possible .LAST files (or an hdf5 file if last_name is provided).
- file 'display_now': write every possible visualization files.
- file 'flush': write content of opened postpro files

concatenate_DISPLAY.name: concatenate_DISPLAY
concatenate_DISPLAY.doc:
Create a paraview pvd format file in /DISPLAY 
from all vtu or vtp display files located in /DDM_WD_*/DISPLAY

concatenate_OUTBOX.name: concatenate_OUTBOX
concatenate_OUTBOX.doc:
Concatenate contents of DDM_WD_*/OUTBOX directories in a single
OUTBOX directory

create_preconW_directory.name: create_preconW_directory
create_preconW_directory.doc: gestion/nettoyage du repertoire de sauvegarde des matrices precon W

create_working_directory.name: create_working_directory
create_working_directory.doc:
Create the needed DATBOX directories for
a number of subdomain.

getInteractions.name: getInteractions
getInteractions.doc:
Get all interactions as a numpy array with predefined dtype.

Must be called after: 'Intialize', 'SetDimension' and 'ReadBehaviours'

By default, get verlet interactions, to get 'this' interaction, change
the eponym parameter to True.

By default, remap parameters id to name and contact law id to its
corresponding name. To keep integer values change 'human' argument
to False.

getInternalArray.name: getInternalArray
getInternalArray.doc:
Get the internal field as an array.

If the field as not been registered with `registerInterInternals`
beforehand, it is automatically registered.

A default value is needed because in case of mixed contact laws,
the desired field may not be defined everywhere.

Parameters
----------
field : string
        The name of the internal field to get
inters : numpy array
         The interaction numpy array from which to extract internal
default : float
          The default value when the internal field is undefined (0.)

pushF2f.name: pushF2f
pushF2f.signature: (f2f_c, f2f_p, f2f_inters, inters, f2f_uf, cop_uf, cpc_uf)

registerInterInternals.name: registerInterInternals
registerInterInternals.doc:
Register an interaction internal fields.

Store a mapping function (numpy vectorized) allowing
to get for a given contact law name, the corresponding
index (starting with 0) in the internals array.

If there is no contact law using the input fields,
the field is still registered but nothing will be done.

Must be called after: ReadBehaviours.

Parameters
----------
fields : string or list of string
         The name(s) of the internal(s) to register.

repack_h5file.name: repack_h5file
repack_h5file.doc: use h5_repack on a HDF5 file to use free unused disk space

save_preconW_one_body.name: save_preconW_one_body
save_preconW_one_body.doc: sauve le matrice precon W d'un corps donne

setInternalArray.name: setInternalArray
setInternalArray.doc:
Set the internal field in 'this' interactions.

If the field as not been registered with `registerInterInternals`
beforehand, it is automatically registered.

Can handle interactions with 'human' or 'compute id' dtype.

Parameters
----------
field : string
        The name of the internal field to get
inters : numpy array
         The interaction numpy array for which to set the internal
internals : numpy array
            The float array with value of internals (same size than inters)
